classification.difficultyReason: Choose and draw the appropriate whole-and-part structure for each operation, distinguishing four equal b parts from one b whole divided into four.

content.prompt: Draw bar models to represent these expressions.

answer.worked: The parts $b$ and $4$ join to make a whole of $b+4$.

spec.description: A whole bar labelled b+4 above two joined parts labelled b and 4.
spec.mathematics: The whole equals the sum of the two parts. Segment widths are illustrative.

answer.short: A whole bar labelled $b$, split into parts $b-4$ and $4$.
answer.worked: The whole is $b$. Removing the part of length $4$ leaves $b-4$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 12b; whole-and-part subtraction models in question 11
spec.description: A whole bar labelled b above two parts labelled b-4 and 4.
spec.mathematics: The remaining part equals the whole minus 4. Segment widths are illustrative.

answer.short: Divide a whole bar labelled $b$ into four equal parts; each part is $\frac{b}{4}$.
answer.worked: Four equal parts make the whole $b$, so each part represents $\frac{b}{4}$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 12c; equal-part bar convention in question 11
spec.description: A whole bar labelled b above four equal parts, each labelled b/4 using stacked fractions.
spec.mathematics: Each of four equal subdivisions of b represents b divided by 4.

answer.short: Join four equal bars, each labelled $b$.
answer.worked: Four equal parts of length $b$ make a whole of $4b$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 12d; repeated equal-part models in question 11
spec.description: A whole bar labelled 4b above four equal parts, each labelled b.
spec.mathematics: Four equal bars of length b have total length 4b.
